text.p: Lumberton, N.C., is struggling to close a $700,000 budget shortfall blamed on lower-than-expected property tax revenues, Fayetteville Observer-Times reported Tuesday.
The city has frozen non-essential hiring and spending, and halted capital spending from its General Fund. It is also considering laying off more than two dozen workers, according to the nespaper.

City Manager Rob Hites said Lumberton had a $1.2 million shortfall in its general fund as of January 1996 but had expected to offset the shortage this year through projected increases in property tax revenues.
Cumberland County Tax Office had predicted property values would grow by 33 percent and Hite budgeted for a 27 percent increase. But the actual increase was only 11.8 percent.
